label: Parcel
description: A parcel of real property as a government cadastral or assessment roll records it — its identity (the parcel or folio number), who is on the roll for it, how it is classified for use, and what it was assessed at. Epistery-published vocabulary: schema.org types places and real-estate listings, not land records. This is the general parcel type; AgParcel (agricultural use) and TaxParcel (a taxing authority's roll, e.g. NYC borough/block/lot) are specializations of the same idea. The parcel identifier is the identity; ownership, use and value are observations against it for a stated roll, and are authoritative only as of that roll.

identity.note: The @id is state, county, and the parcel/folio number. A parcel number is unique only within its county.

fields.name: parcelId
fields.description: The parcel or folio number as the assessing authority's roll records it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: A human label for the parcel, normally its situs (physical) address.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: The owner of record as the roll names them — a person, entity, trust, or estate.

fields.name: useCode
fields.description: The assessing authority's own land-use classification code.

fields.name: useDescription
fields.description: Human-readable land use for that code.

fields.name: marketValue
fields.description: The just/market value the roll assessed for the roll year.

fields.name: yearBuilt
fields.description: Year the primary structure was built.

fields.name: livingArea
fields.description: Heated / living area of the structure.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The government roll this record came from.
fields.example: FL Department of Revenue (statewide parcel + sales export)

fields.name: url
fields.description: The assessing authority's own page for this parcel, when available.

trust.note: Reserved — cadastral proof points (roll year, county/authority of record, assessment or extract date) as the market defines them. A parcel record is authoritative only as of its roll; the vintage belongs here.
